answer: Make every identity guard a unique shard of the shared archive, like a lotus rooted in its own patch of mud: before each epoch, the network assigns each agent a random slice of ledger history to store, then issues random retrieval challenges. A harbor of a thousand fake identities needs a thousand disks holding a thousand distinct shards, because sharing one copy fails every challenge — the canyon between one real disk and a thousand fakes is measured in hardware, not keys. Fail a challenge and the stake is slashed, so cheap copies drown in storage costs.
